name: KY-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district partisan lean in a heavily Republican seat
Massive GOP spending advantage and Polymarket at 97% Republican
Democratic nominee minimally funded with no outside support
Open seat removes Massie's personal brand but not the GOP structural edge
model.rationale: The R+18 lean, the Democrat's negligible fundraising, and heavy Republican outside spending all point to a comfortable GOP hold, and prediction markets price a Republican win at 97%. The open seat adds modest uncertainty but nothing suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: A late scandal or GOP spending collapse in the general could narrow the margin, though a Democratic upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Thomas Massie (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northern Kentucky's 4th District is a strongly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the GOP. Thomas Massie lost renomination, so this is an open-seat contest, but the Republican nominee Ed Gallrein enters with a large financial edge: more than $3.5 million raised plus millions in outside spending on his behalf, against a Democratic opponent who has raised under $100,000 with no outside backing.

Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 97 percent, and no general-election polls suggest competitive conditions. The baseline model expects a Republican margin in the mid-to-high teens. Barring an unforeseen development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin.
